messages:
sophia: Quick idea from intake triage: too many fullbench runs are blocking flow. Suggest a crisp ownership split: infra owns fast runtime/compat checks, ML owns golden sets and deep evals.

liam: +1. To make infra checks deterministic we need a small manifest with tokenizer id/hash, seqlen, artifact path, and a reproducible seed.

maria: ML will provide golden subset + thresholds (ppl delta, exact-match). Can infra define a cheap sampled bench that runs in <10m?

devops-jen: We can run a 300-sample shadow job (fp16 + int8) as part of CI on a small GPU pool. Outputs a compat JSON.

registry-bot: Manifest accepted: /models/m-2607/manifest@sha256:fa7e. link: https://reg.internal/m/m-2607

sophia: Nice. Runtime should also emit a single header x-compat-score (0..100) so rollout-service can subscribe without pulling blobs.

liam: Agree. Define mapping: token_match(0..40) + perf_band(0..40) + kv_flag(0..20) => compat_score. Keep it stable.

maria: ML will publish thresholds in manifest meta. Also add allowed_orgs and kms_key_id for private models.

devops-jen: Ops note: we'll wire automatic rollback to compat_score < 60 OR error_rate > 1%. Need single signal to alert on.

sophia: Action items: maria + liam draft manifest proto (Weds), devops-jen prototype shadow smoke job (next Tue), sophia will write a short RFC for ownership (Fri).

liam: Also include tokenizer_hash + repro_seed in manifest so ML benches are replayable.

maria: I'll open PR for manifest and attach a tiny example manifest snippet.

sophia: Thanks all. Sync Fri 09:30 to review PR and prototype. End of thread.
